messages:
zoe_marketing: Hey runtime team  small but important ask for the launch blog + webinar. We need a compact, reproducible bench sanity pack with a short correction mapping to prod so we can confidently cite numbers.

zoe_marketing: Scope: 600 anonymized samples stratified by token length (0-64 / 65-256 / 257-1024). Run variants: fp16, int8. Measures: gen p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, est cost per 1M tokens; embed p95 for med slice; one end-to-end rerank trace (embed all candidates + top-k generate). Include coldstart (pod restart) and warmed runs (5 warmups).

zoe_marketing: Deliverables: CSV (variant,slice,run_type,p50_ms,p95_ms,p99_ms,tps,est_cost_per_1M_tokens), 3-bullet summary, runner-config, warmup seed list, and one demo trace. Also please add a small table that maps staging A10g->prod A100 expected delta (+/- %). ETA: EOD Wed?

raj_runtime: We can do this. Couple clarifiers: (1) do you want a separate low-latency batching profile (max_batch_size=8) vs default? (2) should the prod correction be a rough note or a calibrated multiplier from prior runs?

zoe_marketing: Yes to low-latency profile (we need the webinar stat). For prod correction, a calibrated multiplier is ideal if you have historical A10g->A100 deltas; otherwise a conservative note is fine.

lina_eng-runtime: Running on staging (A10g). Plan: 3 repeats per variant, coldstart uses full pod restart, warm = 5 per-worker warmups. We'll run low-latency and default batching. If p95 variance >10% we'll rerun with fixed seeds and capture heatmap of seq_len vs latency.

devops-bot: Deploy job scheduled: bench-2312349999 queued on staging at 2026-02-25T09:30:00Z. Job id: bench-2312349999.

raj_runtime: Coldstart sweep complete (prelim): redwood-v1-base(fp16) p95 = 215ms(0-64), 360ms(65-256), 980ms(257-1024). int8 shows ~13% lower p95 on med slice. Note: long slice p95 variance was ~14% across repeats due to occasional GC pauses and one worker OOM on int8 long runs. We're investigating.

zoe_marketing: Hmm — the long-slice variance is concerning for the blog. If it's OOM-related can you capture the error trace and try a second pass with smaller max_batch_size for long slice to show stabilized numbers?

raj_runtime: Yep. We'll rerun long slice with max_batch_size=12 and low-latency (8) profiles. ETA 2 hours. We'll keep raw traces and include an explanatory note in the summary.

lina_eng-runtime: Rerun results: with max_batch_size=12 the long-slice p95 stabilized to 940ms and variance dropped to ~6%. int8 remains ~12% faster on med. We also saw that enabling prefix KV cache for warmed runs drops med p95 by ~8%. We'll document both.

clara_marketing: For the webinar slide we want one crisp stat: exact % improvement p95 int8 vs fp16 on 256-token median payload (warmed). Can you paste that micro-run?

raj_runtime: Micro-run (256-token median, warmed, median of 3): fp16 p95 = 345ms, int8 p95 = 305ms -> ~11.6% reduction. tokens/sec fp16 = 240 t/s, int8 = 275 t/s. est cost/1M tokens fp16 = $11.80, int8 = $10.45 (staging rates).

josh_product: Can you also include a one-line reproducibility blurb for the blog and the runner-config we used? Product wants to paste it verbatim into the methodology box.

raj_runtime: One-liner: "Measured on staging (A10g) with anonymized stratified inputs; reported values are medians over 3 runs. See attached traces and runner-config for full reproducibility."

raj_runtime: Runner-config snippet:
```
workers: 8
batching_profiles:
  default: { max_batch_size: 24, max_tokens: 2048 }
  low_latency: { max_batch_size: 8, max_tokens: 1024 }
warmup:
  per_worker: 5
seed_list: bench-2312349999-seeds.txt
repeats: 3
```

raj_runtime: Uploaded bundle: s3://redwood-staging/bench-2312349999/bundle.zip (CSV, runner-config, warmup seed list, raw traces, demo trace). Also included a short correction table: "A10g->A100 expected gen p95 improvement: +10-20% (depends on batch mix and seq length); see correction_notes.txt in bundle."

zoe_marketing: Fantastic  thanks. We'll use the warmed med micro-run for the slide and add the correction footnote. Please keep the bundle and tag me once it's copied into the launch repo.

devops-bot: Upload complete: s3://redwood-staging/bench-2312349999/bundle.zip. checksum: d4f9e8a1.

raj_runtime: Tagged you on the s3 folder and added a 2-bullet summary in summary.txt: (1) int8 reduces warmed med p95 ~11-13% vs fp16; (2) long-slice instability fixed by reducing batch size for long requests. If you need any additional micro-slices for the keynote demo, we can run quick follow-ups.

zoe_marketing: Perfect  we'll draft the slide + blog and request final sign-off tomorrow. Thanks everyone! :rocket:
